name: What is involved in designing an accessible zero-threshold walk-in shower?

mainEntity.name: What is involved in designing an accessible zero-threshold walk-in shower?

acceptedAnswer.text: Installing an accessible, barrier-free walk-in shower requires eliminating the standard curb to create a seamless transition from the bathroom floor. This curb-free design often involves recessing the shower floor into the subfloor so water drains properly toward a linear or center drain without spilling into the main room. Remodeling plans can also incorporate sturdy blocking behind drywall for grab bars, non-slip textured floor tiles, built-in seating, and handheld shower wands positioned at reachable heights.
acceptedAnswer.description: Accessible walk-in showers require recessing the floor for curbless entry, installing a properly sloped drain, adding structural wall blocking for grab bars, and choosing non-slip flooring.
